headline: Bangla song ‘Jodi Lokkho Thake Otut’ featured on FIFA World Cup page
summary: The official FIFA World Cup Facebook page has shared a Bengali song, sparking emotional reactions from artists and fans.
details: The official Facebook page of the FIFA World Cup has featured the Bengali song ‘Jodi Lokkho Thake Otut’.
The song, which focuses on perseverance and determination, has gained significant attention on the global platform.
Asif Iqbal, one of the artists involved, expressed an emotional reaction to seeing the song on the official FIFA page.
This rare recognition of a Bengali song on a major international sports platform has brought pride to music lovers in Bangladesh.

headline_marked: Parliament [[passes Cyber Security amendment bill]], drops gambling clause
headline: Parliament passes Cyber Security amendment bill, drops gambling clause
summary: The Cyber Security (amendment) Bill, 2026, removes Section-20, which previously mandated tougher action against online gambling.
details: Parliament has passed the Cyber Security (amendment) Bill, 2026, removing Section-20, which mandated tougher action for online gambling and other crimes in cyberspace.

Posts, Telecommunications and Information Technology Minister Faqir Mahbub Anam tabled the bill on Tuesday. The proposal was initially rejected by voice votes before being endorsed by parliament members.
The gambling clause was omitted because a separate law, the Gambling Prevention Bill-2026, has been adopted to handle such crimes.
Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed clarified that with the new Gambling Prevention Bill, there is no longer a need to include gambling-related sections in the cyber security law.
During the session, demands were raised to ensure the safety of women in cyberspace.
Opposition MPs also warned the government against using the law to suppress dissent or harass citizens.
caption:
Bangladesh's parliament has amended the Cyber Security law, removing the online gambling clause.

Parliament has passed the Cyber Security (amendment) Bill, 2026, removing Section-20, which mandated tougher action for online gambling and other crimes in cyberspace.

Posts, Telecommunications and Information Technology Minister Faqir Mahbub Anam tabled the bill on Tuesday. The proposal was initially rejected by voice votes before being endorsed by parliament members.

The gambling clause was omitted because a separate law, the Gambling Prevention Bill-2026, has been adopted to handle such crimes.

Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed clarified that with the new Gambling Prevention Bill, there is no longer a need to include gambling-related sections in the cyber security law.

During the session, demands were raised to ensure the safety of women in cyberspace.

Opposition MPs also warned the government against using the law to suppress dissent or harass citizens.

#Bangladesh #CyberSecurity #Parliament #LawAmendment #DigitalSafety

Source: bdnews24.com, Somoy News, Dhaka Tribune
